title: Equidistribution of Prime-Degree Torus Packets with Arbitrary Local Type
main_claim: For fixed prime n>=5 and any sequence (K_i, M_i, sigma_i) of totally real degree-n fields with full lattices of arbitrary local homothety type and D(M_i)->infinity, the volume-weighted packet measures converge weakly to Haar measure on SL_n(Z)\SL_n(R), with no escape of mass.

issues.location: entropy.tex, Prop. entropy-from-balls; Measure classification paragraph; analytic.tex Lemma residue
issues.description: Three external results are used as paraphrases and I did not check them against the original papers: the ELMV09 Cor. 3.3 tube/Bowen-ball entropy criterion (conventions for B^{(s,t)} and the factor 2 eta), Stark's Lemmas 3 and 8 (zero-free box, and that an exceptional zero forces a quadratic subfield, constant 4 n!), and EKL06 Cor. 1.4 (for prime n, positive entropy plus ergodicity gives Haar). The way the paper uses each one is consistent with the standard statements.
issues.evidence: With mass(xT_t) <= C e^{-lambda t} and eta = lambda/3, the criterion's required bound C e^{-2 eta t} holds with room to spare, so even a factor-2 difference in the Bowen-ball convention would not matter. Odd n rules out quadratic subfields, so Stark's alternative cannot occur.

coverage: Read every section (packets, local, analytic, geometry, entropy, adelic appendix) line by line. Checked: (1) packet parametrization: covol sigma(N) = Q N(I); the bijection modulo the E-action, including -1 identifying opposite sign components and its match with W_n for odd n; vol(F) = 2^{n-1} R_K and h vol F = sqrt(D) kappa from the class number formula with w=2. (2) Unfolding: free E-orbit fibers, the normalized product N((alpha)I^{-1})/Q, Jacobian 1, the coefficient 1/(sqrt(D) kappa), and that the containment probability equals P((alpha)I^{-1}) under unit Haar measure, which pushes forward to uniform measure on the local choices. (3) Local lemma: valuation-shell masses Z_l^{-1}/d give sum P/d = Z_S/q exactly; R_l L_l = R_l gives a unit in each component projection, hence the tail Pr(v_p >= k) <= l^{-ceil(k/e)}; a union bound gives Pr(j >= a) <= n l^{-a}; ns = 1/2 gives the moment bound 1 + C l^{-1/2}; the product over S is << q^eps; the tail is Q^{-s/16}/q. (4) Residue lemma: Hadamard identity with r1 = n, the ratio bound for Re 1/(sigma - rho) (verified, constant (1+1/c)^2 <= stated), F'/F = O(L), and kappa >> 1/L. (5) Weighted count: u >= Q^{5/8} >= D^{1/4} puts h = 1/log u in range; Shiu's interval condition holds; Euler-factor removal at S matches log Z_S up to O(1); the large-d tail is o(kappa x/q) because kappa^{-1} << log Q. (6) Cusp: simplex volume (log(X/Na))^{n-1}/(n-1)!, the Abel/Tonelli step, and the resulting theta^n bound. (7) Ball bound: box -> interval of norms of length ~rQ -> r^n, with the Portmanteau order of limits handled correctly. (8) Tube entries: the min of e^{+-(lambda_i - lambda_j)t} bounds, the determinant argument, a cover by r^{-(n-1)} balls of radius Cr giving mass << e^{-lambda t}, and the dominated-measure argument that excludes a positive-weight set of zero-entropy ergodic components. (9) D(M) <= D q^{2n}. The adelic appendix is not used in the main proof; I read it but did not check it in depth.
sibling_notes: Family 015 siblings (quartic, rank 319; sextic, rank 70) also reported no_gap_found and flagged the same paraphrased use of Stark Lemma 8 and ELMV Cor. 3.3. This paper uses the same Stark/Shiu residue-relative counting. Its new ingredient is the arbitrary-local-type weight lemma (local.tex), which I verified fully.
